title: Dependency model (S4 dependency lens's second artifact)
description: docs/decisions/011: edge criticality, the extra-nine rule, and the error-budget split between a service's own failures and its dependencies' failures -- not expressible as design_fragment's flat signal list, the same reasoning that gave the slo lens its own slo_spec artifact (docs/decisions/020). Emitted alongside design_fragment (lenses[].emits).

surface_point_ids.description: Which surface_map.json points this model covers -- the http_client_call/queue_producer points a dependency edge is detected at.

criticality.description: hard: the calling request fails if this dependency fails (the extra-nine rule applies). soft: the calling request can still succeed in a degraded form (the rule does not apply -- a soft dependency's own reliability is a separate, independent concern).

own_target.description: This service's own SLO target for the journey that calls this dependency -- cross-references an slo_spec's objective.target when one covers the same journey, restated here so this artifact is self-contained and gate-checkable without a cross-artifact lookup.

required_dependency_target.description: The minimum reliability this dependency itself must hit for a hard edge -- gate-verified (oah/design/dependency_gates.py) to be at least one nine better than own_target, i.e. its own failure rate (1 - target) at most one-tenth of own_target's failure rate. A dependency less reliable than its dependent leaves no real error-budget room for the dependent's own bugs.

budget_split.description: How this journey's own error budget is partitioned between its own bugs and this dependency's failures -- the two fractions must sum to 1.0 (gate-verified), so the split is a real accounting, not two independent guesses.

fallback_behavior.description: What actually happens when this dependency fails -- retry, circuit-break, degrade, or (for a hard edge with no fallback) an explicit statement that failure propagates. Required for every edge, hard or soft.
